_comment: Agencies the registry cannot hold, written in by hand. The registry (../ny-gov-web-registry) lists 317 agencies and marks EVERY one status:'active'; its relations/mandates/founding_date/dissolution_date fields are filled in for ZERO of them (measured 2026-08-26). So a body that was shut down - DoITT, the 1998 City of New York Technology Steering Committee, a task force wound up after its report - can only live here. This file is what makes lineage tracing possible, and it is filled in by hand from the review list that the new-name pass produces, never automatically.
_schema: Same shape as a registry agency: id, name, short_name, other_names[]. Plus 'provenance', which MUST name at least one eo_id whose text shows the name in use - a name with no source order does not belong here (README: 'a guess is a bug').

_example.name: Department of Information Technology and Telecommunications

entities.name: Department of Information Technology and Telecommunications

provenance.note: Merges into the existing registry agency 'oti' rather than standing on its own, because MODA says the same thing: record NYC_GOID_000382 (Office of Technology and Innovation) lists 'Department of Information Technology and Telecommunications' under alternate_or_former_names and 'DoITT' under alternate_or_former_acronyms. Those two values are the ONLY ones out of all 306 MODA records that ../ny-gov-web-registry is missing (diffed by nyc_goid, 2026-08-26). The cause is upstream: the 'oti' record has provenance.sources ['manual','greenbook'] with no 'moda', so build_registry.py never merged it, even though the nyc_goid identifier is attached. DELETE THIS ENTRY once that is fixed upstream and the registry is re-synced.
eo_evidence: 2006-EO-098: "the Commissioner of the Department of Information Technology and Telecommunications (DoITT)"
2014-EO-008: "The Commissioner of the Department of Information Technology and Telecommunications (DoITT)"
2008-EO-115: "the Department of Information Technology and Telecommunications (“DOITT”)" — the all-capitals spelling is how the order is set, not OCR damage
1995-EO-025: earliest use of the long name in the corpus
2022-EO-003: the order that hands DoITT's work to OTI
